editorial_reason: ProofWiki formally constructs integers as the inverse completion of natural numbers. This equivalence relation is independent of rational numbers and gives explicit representatives without assuming integer subtraction already exists. The induced addition and multiplication require separate well-definedness checks, so this is an independently described construction, not a proof the resulting quotient is an integral domain.

The dedicated ProofWiki ring-of-integers definition introduces the integer ring and directs readers to theorems that verify its ring and integral-domain properties. The structural assertion that (Z,+,·) is an integral domain is a theorem/property, not itself the definition of integer ring; it must remain distinguishable in publication from the bare named structure.

Stacks Project Example 9.3.4 gives explicit fraction equivalence and the universal property; ProofWiki gives an independently checked field-of-quotients formulation involving an injective embedding into a field. The construction requires D to be an integral domain to support the equivalence criterion and well-defined inverses of nonzero classes. Q is the instance D=Z; general fraction fields and total quotient rings for rings with zero divisors are not the same context.
